Switzerland travel FAQ

Quick answers to the questions first-time visitors ask most. Follow the links for full guides and official sources.

Entry & Planning

Do I need a visa to visit Switzerland?

Many short-term tourists can enter Switzerland visa-free for up to 90 days with a valid passport. Always verify current entry and electronic travel authorization rules on the official consulate website before flying.

How many days do I need for a first trip to Switzerland?

10 to 14 days is ideal for seeing 3 or 4 major regions without rushing, though a focused 7-day trip covering Zurich and Lucerne is also very rewarding.

Trains & Transport

Should I buy a rail pass or individual SBB CFF FFS & Panoramic Alpine Railways tickets?

Compare both using our Rail Pass Calculator. Point-to-point early-bird tickets are often cheaper for 2–3 cities, while passes shine on multi-stop loops.

Can I bring large suitcases on SBB CFF FFS & Panoramic Alpine Railways trains?

Yes, standard suitcases fit on overhead racks or in end-of-car luggage racks. Check our Luggage Size Checker for exact dimensions.

Money & Cards

Is Switzerland mostly cash or card?

Contactless cards (Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay, Google Pay) are accepted at almost all hotels, train stations, supermarkets, and restaurants, though carrying 50–100 in CHF (Swiss Franc) cash is wise for small markets and rural buses.

What is the tipping custom in Switzerland?

Check our Etiquette & Tipping Checker for situasi-by-situation advice across restaurants, taxis, and hotels in Switzerland.

Practical & Safety

What power plugs and voltage does Switzerland use?

Switzerland uses Type J & Type C (230V / 50Hz). Modern phone and laptop chargers (100–240V) only need a plug adapter.

What is the emergency phone number in Switzerland?

In an emergency in Switzerland, dial 112 (General Emergency), 144 (Ambulance), 1414 (REGA Mountain Rescue), 117 (Police).
